pr.title: Plan reviewing pull requests in GitHub Actions
pr.head: e5497eec71fefa1dab3091eda06f646523e7c150

summary: Projector currently needs a live agent session to review a pull request. This plan moves the same review method into GitHub Actions, so ready pull requests can receive a labeled verdict and a review page while no session is running.

The first version adds a headless command, a composite action, repository setup, and review-account configuration. A separate job publishes summaries with the writing token; the agent receives only a token that can read repository contents and write review results.

cards.title: Implementation boundary
cards.html:
• The plan is ready with priority now; this pull request adds no runner or workflow implementation.
  • Fork pull requests remain excluded, and the existing approval setting stays in force.
  • Hosted-runner authentication and API behavior are explicitly deferred to rollout checks.
  • App credentials, context repositories, and a self-hosted reviewer follow the initial rollout.

cards.title: Review follow-up
cards.html: The revised plan addresses all three earlier findings: the runner rejects forks and drafts for every trigger, visibility reads remain allowed, and unknown visibility cannot authorize private context. The current head has a clean review; hosted-runner behavior remains an implementation check.

groups.title: Run and publish a review in CI
groups.kicker: The execution, identity, persistence, and trust contract for unattended reviews
intro: The new project review run command launches Claude or Codex without interactive prompts, then verifies that the agent published a verdict for the selected head. A composite action restores the prior review record so small pushes can use incremental review, which builds on the last full review.

A second job receives the agent’s summary as an artifact and publishes it with its own token. Repository setup writes the workflow and reviewer settings, and asks GitHub’s CLI to collect the model credential. Eligibility checks run before an agent starts, and private context needs confirmed nonpublic visibility for both repositories.

files.note: Defines the ready CI-review plan, its runner presets, two-job publication flow, setup command, acceptance tests, and rollout decisions.

checks.text: Project discovery reports ready/now, project check passes, and section 7 explicitly decides or defers each listed question.
Read the revised runner sequence: forks and drafts exit before reading a diff, posting, or starting an agent. Predicate checks reject both cases for manual and pull request triggers.
Compared the preset rules: gh repo view is explicitly allowed and no longer matches the mutation deny list; gh repo edit remains denied.
Checked the revised visibility conditions with unknown, public, and private values. An unknown target cannot admit private context, and an unknown context is always excluded.
The exact-head gate passed plugin validation, 247 hook tests, hook type checking, whitespace checks, and the configured GitHub Actions check. The planned runner itself is still unimplemented.
